Repeatable Modelling Workflow

Kim Cressman

created 2022-02-08; latest update 2025-11-10

library(readxl)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(lmerTest)
library(MuMIn)
library(boot)
library(tibble)

# cost function for sMdAPE (symmetric median absolute percent error)  
# works on square-root transformed response variable  
cost <- function(obs, expt){
    median(
        abs(
            100 * (obs^2-expt^2) / ((obs^2+expt^2)/2)
        )
    )
}

This document pulls together all the model-running and coefficient-presenting code, by using previous scripts as child documents.

Data Import and Summaries

A few notes.

  • NIW collected tank samples from one site and ISCO samples from a different site. Due to their concerns about pooling data from the two sites (they are very different environments), I created a ‘NIW_isco’ reserve ID to differentiate.
  • For a similar reason, I created a ‘HEE_w2’ reserve ID for the site where He’eia started getting samples for this project, but the water is so clear that the sensor wasn’t working well. Figured I’d separate it out.
  • GRB used 8 different stations throughout. I did not differentiate. If models fit poorly for this reserve, this could be a reason.
  • PDB used 3 differents stations, and again I did not differentiate.
  • I made up a station ID for Sapelo because they did not use a normal SWMP station. I called it ‘sapnawq’ (for ‘N/A’, ha)

In this file

  • Data will be subsetted to a data frame that does not contain ANY NAs, because model selection is based on models containing exactly the same input data.
  • That subset will be saved as an .Rdata file for easier import and reuse downstream.
  • Some summary statistics for the data that will be used will be generated.

Data import and export

re-run 12/16/2021 to incorporate new data file sent on 12/15 (GRB ISCO data had been left out of original file)

update 2/16/2022 to incorporate temperature-corrected RFU (based on Hannah Ramage’s calculations) into the modeling data frame. The “global” rho is an average of the rho values in all of the temperature-interference trials. The global rho is then inserted into the Watras et al. 2017 Eq. 1:

Temp-corrected-RFU = original-RFU / (1 + global_rho*(temp_reading - 20))

I’m hardcoding in the rhos here because it’s easier than dealing with another file, but am setting up the code to be rerun easily with a different batch of rhos (however they’re read in).

rhos <- c(-0.018449239,
-0.017224308,
-0.006810888,
-0.017013983,
-0.016389726,
-0.016809971,
-0.010759556,
-0.011669893,
-0.006993083,
-0.010889714,
-0.0081596,
-0.002334279
)

global_rho <- mean(rhos)

dat <- read_xlsx(here::here("data", "2021_chla-catalyst_data_all.xlsx"),
                 sheet = "qaqc") %>% 
    mutate(extracted = chla_ugl,
           sensor_rfu = chlorophyll_rfu,
           sensor_ugl = chl_fluor,
           month = lubridate::month(datetime_collected),
           season = case_when(month %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "Winter",
                              month %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "Spring",
                              month %in% c(6, 7, 8)   ~ "Summer",
                              month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall")) %>% 
    select(reserve = reserve_code,
           station = station_code,
           datetime_collected,
           month,
           season,
           method,
           extracted,
           sensor_rfu,
           temp,
           turb,
           fdom_qsu) %>% 
    mutate(station = case_when(reserve == "GND" ~ "gndblwq",
                               reserve == "SAP" ~ "sapnawq",
                               TRUE ~ station),
           reserve = case_when(station == "heew2wq" ~ "HEE_w2",
                               station == "WS" ~ "NIW_isco", # at NIW: OL is tank; WS is ISCO. These should not be pooled.
                               TRUE ~ reserve),
           station = case_when(station == "OL" ~ "niwolwq",
                               station == "WS" ~ "niwwswq",
                               TRUE ~ station)) %>% 
    drop_na() %>% 
    mutate(across(c(reserve, month, season),
                  as.factor),
           season = forcats::fct_relevel(season, c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),
           rfu_temp_corrected = sensor_rfu / (1 + global_rho*(temp-20)))

save(dat, file = here::here("data", "subset_no_NA.RData"))

Exploring Possible Transformations of Response

Fitting a linear model with all possible predictors, then evaluating residuals and predictive performance in a rough way to see which transformation works best. This exploration led to the decision to use a square-root transformation and all following model selection will be based on square-root transformation of the response variable (extracted chlorophyll).

# library(readxl)
# library(dplyr)
# library(tidyr)
# library(ggplot2)
# library(patchwork)
# 
load(here::here("data", "subset_no_NA.RData"))

# original plot settings, for later
op <- par()

Full Model with all interactions

response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + month + reserve

No transformation of response

Fit Model

full <- lm(extracted ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + month + reserve, data = dat)

# diagnostics
df_untransf <- broom::glance(full)

Plot residuals

par(mfrow = c(2, 2),
    mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
plot(full)

Square-root transformation of response

Fit Model

full_sqrt <- lm(sqrt(extracted) ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + month + reserve, data = dat)

# diagnostics  
df_sqrt <- broom::glance(full_sqrt)

Plot residuals

par(mfrow = c(2, 2),
    mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
plot(full_sqrt)

Fourth-root transformation of response

Similar to a natural-log transformation, but log(0) doesn’t exist so I’d like to avoid that transformation.

Fit Model

full_frthrt <- lm(extracted^0.25 ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + month + reserve, data = dat)

# diagnostics
df_frthrt <- broom::glance(full_frthrt)

Plot residuals

par(mfrow = c(2, 2),
    mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
plot(full_frthrt)

Log transformation of response

Because this is common and I got asked about it in a Data Team meeting.

Fit Model

full_log10 <- lm(log10(extracted + 0.1) ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + month + reserve, data = dat)

# diagnostics
df_log10 <- broom::glance(full_log10)

Plot residuals

par(mfrow = c(2, 2),
    mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
plot(full_log10)

Diagnostics and predictions for all

Predictions use exponents to get them back on the original scale.

dat_preds <- dat %>% 
    mutate(preds_full_untr = fitted.values(full),
           preds_full_sqrt = (fitted.values(full_sqrt))^2,
           preds_full_frthrt = (fitted.values(full_frthrt))^4,
           preds_full_log10 = 10^(fitted.values(full_log10)),
           
           abs_dev_untr = abs(preds_full_untr - extracted),
           abs_dev_sqrt = abs(preds_full_sqrt - extracted),
           abs_dev_frthrt = abs(preds_full_frthrt - extracted),
           abs_dev_log10 = abs(preds_full_log10 - extracted))

fits <- tribble(
    ~"transformation", ~"R2", ~"AdjR2", ~"MedAbsDev",
    "none", df_untransf$r.squared, df_untransf$adj.r.squared, median(dat_preds$abs_dev_untr),
    "square-root", df_sqrt$r.squared, df_sqrt$adj.r.squared, median(dat_preds$abs_dev_sqrt),
    "fourth-root", df_frthrt$r.squared, df_frthrt$adj.r.squared, median(dat_preds$abs_dev_frthrt),
    "log10(x+0.1)", df_log10$r.squared, df_log10$adj.r.squared,
    median(dat_preds$abs_dev_log10)
)

Square-root transformation seems to do the best walking-the-line to get:

  • no negative predictions for extracted chlorophyll
  • generally okay linear fit without extreme prediction outliers or harsh transformation

Initial data and model exploration (not shown in this document; see instead the older 01_first_models_and_transformations files) suggested that distinguishing between ISCO and tank samples at a site did not improve the model (no better AIC than lumping). However, due to huge anecdotal differences at two reserves (GTM and LKS) and the potential for differences at other reserves, models will be run both ways: with all data (Tank + ISCO), and with tank-only data.

Models + Graphics: All Reserves Combined; Tank + ISCO

load(here::here("data", "subset_no_NA.RData"))
# dat <- filter(dat, method == "tank")

# original plot settings, for later
op <- par()

# options, for MuMIn operations
# will prevent fitting sub-models to different datasets (from help file)
options(na.action = "na.fail")
# create "response" column  
dat$response <- sqrt(dat$extracted)

Modeling: All Reserves, Tank + ISCO

At one point, I coded LMMs. But they are very data-hungry and based on 05_model_selection_combined_reserves, didn’t seem to make very different predictions. In theory they are better for various reasons but we are proceeding with only Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) models here.

Each of the models described below are fitted and evaluated using symmetric Median Absolute Percent Error.

n (number of points in the dataset): 1076

from 14 reserves

Full Model

Includes all interactions between sensor_rfu, turbidity, and FDOM. Additionally, temp*rfu and temp*fdom. Hoping we can actually drop some of these.

Reserve included as fixed effect.

response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season + reserve

No FDOM

If we drop FDOM and all its interactions, what do we get?

NOTE this still includes both reserve and season (as well as sensor readings from temp and turbidity)

RFU only

This does not include reserve or season. If the other models above are better, reserve or season could still be the reason (vs. turbidity/temp/FDOM corrections). It would mean local factors still have to be accounted for and modelled to get the most out of a TAL sensor.

# Changed coding to be more similar to the individual reserve files; re-ran using all NIW data lumped together (and all HEE data lumped together) - got same coefficients as before. Individual reserve files use leave-one-out cross-validation, but here I'm using 10-fold because otherwise it's a lot.  

set.seed(1216)
full_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season + reserve, data = dat)

no_fdom_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season + reserve, data = dat)

no_fdom_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season + reserve, data = dat)


rfu_only <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = dat)
rfu_only_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = dat)

sel <- dredge(full_ols, 
              fixed = "sensor_rfu",
              extra = c("R^2", "AdjR^2" = function(x) summary(x)$adj.r.squared))

# perform 10-fold cross-validation on top model to find median prediction error
# cost function is sMdAPE; defined in parent Rmd
ols.1 <- get.models(sel, 1)[[1]]
ols.cv <- cv.glm(dat, ols.1, cost, K = 10)

no_fdom.cv <- cv.glm(dat, no_fdom_ols, cost, K = 10)
no_fdom.df <- data.frame(model.sel(no_fdom_ols))
no_fdom.df$pred_test_error <- round(no_fdom.cv$delta[1], 2)

rfu_only.cv <- cv.glm(dat, rfu_only, cost, K = 10)
rfu_only.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_only))
rfu_only.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_only.cv$delta[1], 2)

# pull out R^2s from lms (glms were run for cross-validation but really they're just regular linear models)
no_fdom.df$R.2 <- round(summary(no_fdom_lm)$r.squared, 4)
rfu_only.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_only_lm)$r.squared, 4)


# only top one
subdf <- data.frame(sel[1])
subdf$pred_test_error <- round(ols.cv$delta[1], 2)
subdf <- subdf %>% 
  bind_rows(no_fdom.df, rfu_only.df) %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "model") %>% 
  mutate(model = case_when(model == "...1" ~ "best_AIC",
                           TRUE ~ model)) %>% 
  select(model, AICc, R.2, pred_test_error, everything()) %>% 
  select(-c(delta, weight))

Summary Table for main models

coeffs <- subdf %>%  
    select(reserve, model, AICc, R.2, prediction_error = pred_test_error,
           sensor_rfu, fdom_qsu, turb, temp, season,
           everything()) %>% 
    mutate(across(c(AICc, prediction_error), round, 2),
           across(c(R.2, sensor_rfu, X.Intercept.), round, 3),
           across(c(fdom_qsu, turb, temp), round, 4),
           across(c(fdom_qsu.sensor_rfu:fdom_qsu.sensor_rfu.turb), round, 4) )

load(here::here("data", "subset_no_NA.RData"))
dat <- filter(dat, method == "tank")

# original plot settings, for later
op <- par()

# options, for MuMIn operations
# will prevent fitting sub-models to different datasets (from help file)
options(na.action = "na.fail")
# create "response" column  
dat$response <- sqrt(dat$extracted)

Modeling: All Reserves, Tank Only

At one point, I coded LMMs. But they are very data-hungry and based on 05_model_selection_combined_reserves, didn’t seem to make very different predictions. In theory they are better for various reasons but we are proceeding with only Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) models here.

Each of the models described below are fitted and evaluated using symmetric Median Absolute Percent Error.

n (number of points in the dataset): 311

from 10 reserves

Full Model

Includes all interactions between sensor_rfu, turbidity, and FDOM. Additionally, temp*rfu and temp*fdom. Hoping we can actually drop some of these.

Reserve included as fixed effect.

response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season + reserve

No FDOM

If we drop FDOM and all its interactions, what do we get?

NOTE this still includes both reserve and season (as well as sensor readings from temp and turbidity)

RFU only

This does not include reserve or season. If the other models above are better, reserve or season could still be the reason (vs. turbidity/temp/FDOM corrections). It would mean local factors still have to be accounted for and modeled to get the most out of a TAL sensor.

RFU + season

Temp-Corrected RFU + season

Temp-corrected RFU is denoted as tc_rfu in the model names and objects. The correction was based on a global rho value which was the average of all individual rho values, as calculated by Hannah Ramage, from the temperature interference trials. This global rho value was then inserted into the equation from Watras et al. 2017 as follows:

Temp-corrected-RFU = original-RFU / (1 + global_rho*(temp_reading - 20))

# Changed coding to be more similar to the individual reserve files; re-ran using all NIW data lumped together (and all HEE data lumped together) - got same coefficients as before. Individual reserve files use leave-one-out cross-validation, but here I'm using 10-fold because otherwise it's a lot. 

# 2/16/22 adding some new models of interest, and really wishing I'd somehow made everything below into a function. Still not sure how, but it would have helped a lot.

set.seed(1216)
full_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season + reserve, data = dat)

no_fdom_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season + reserve, data = dat)

no_fdom_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season + reserve, data = dat)

rfu_only <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = dat)
rfu_only_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = dat)

rfu_season <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + season, data = dat)
rfu_season_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + season, data = dat)

rfu_reserve <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + reserve, data = dat)
rfu_reserve_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + reserve, data = dat)

rfu_season_res <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + season + reserve, data = dat)
rfu_season_res_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + season + reserve, data = dat)

tc_rfu_season <- glm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + season, data = dat)
tc_rfu_season_lm <- lm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + season, data = dat)

tc_rfu_reserve <- glm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + reserve, data = dat)
tc_rfu_reserve_lm <- lm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + reserve, data = dat)

tc_rfu_season_res <- glm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + season + reserve, data = dat)
tc_rfu_season_res_lm <- lm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + season + reserve, data = dat)

sel <- dredge(full_ols, 
              fixed = "sensor_rfu",
              extra = c("R^2", "AdjR^2" = function(x) summary(x)$adj.r.squared))

# perform 10-fold cross-validation on top model to find median prediction error
# cost function is sMdAPE; defined in parent Rmd
ols.1 <- get.models(sel, 1)[[1]]
ols.cv <- cv.glm(dat, ols.1, cost, K = 10)

no_fdom.cv <- cv.glm(dat, no_fdom_ols, cost, K = 10)
no_fdom.df <- data.frame(model.sel(no_fdom_ols))
no_fdom.df$pred_test_error <- round(no_fdom.cv$delta[1], 2)

rfu_only.cv <- cv.glm(dat, rfu_only, cost, K = 10)
rfu_only.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_only))
rfu_only.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_only.cv$delta[1], 2)

rfu_season.cv <- cv.glm(dat, rfu_season, cost, K = 10)
rfu_season.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_season))
rfu_season.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_season.cv$delta[1], 2)

rfu_reserve.cv <- cv.glm(dat, rfu_reserve, cost, K = 10)
rfu_reserve.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_reserve))
rfu_reserve.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_reserve.cv$delta[1], 2)

rfu_season_res.cv <- cv.glm(dat, rfu_season_res, cost, K = 10)
rfu_season_res.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_season_res))
rfu_season_res.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_season_res.cv$delta[1], 2)

tc_rfu_season.cv <- cv.glm(dat, tc_rfu_season, cost, K = 10)
tc_rfu_season.df <- data.frame(model.sel(tc_rfu_season))
tc_rfu_season.df$pred_test_error <- round(tc_rfu_season.cv$delta[1], 2)

tc_rfu_reserve.cv <- cv.glm(dat, tc_rfu_reserve, cost, K = 10)
tc_rfu_reserve.df <- data.frame(model.sel(tc_rfu_reserve))
tc_rfu_reserve.df$pred_test_error <- round(tc_rfu_reserve.cv$delta[1], 2)

tc_rfu_season_res.cv <- cv.glm(dat, tc_rfu_season_res, cost, K = 10)
tc_rfu_season_res.df <- data.frame(model.sel(tc_rfu_season_res))
tc_rfu_season_res.df$pred_test_error <- round(tc_rfu_season_res.cv$delta[1], 2)


# pull out R^2s from lms (glms were run for cross-validation but really they're just regular linear models)
no_fdom.df$R.2 <- round(summary(no_fdom_lm)$r.squared, 4)
rfu_only.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_only_lm)$r.squared, 4)
rfu_season.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_season_lm)$r.squared, 4)
rfu_reserve.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_reserve_lm)$r.squared, 4)
rfu_season_res.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_season_res_lm)$r.squared, 4)
tc_rfu_season.df$R.2 <- round(summary(tc_rfu_season_lm)$r.squared, 4)
tc_rfu_reserve.df$R.2 <- round(summary(tc_rfu_reserve_lm)$r.squared, 4)
tc_rfu_season_res.df$R.2 <- round(summary(tc_rfu_season_res_lm)$r.squared, 4)

# only top one
subdf <- data.frame(sel[1])
subdf$pred_test_error <- round(ols.cv$delta[1], 2)
subdf <- subdf %>% 
  bind_rows(no_fdom.df, rfu_only.df, 
            rfu_season.df, rfu_reserve.df, rfu_season_res.df,
            tc_rfu_season.df, tc_rfu_reserve.df, tc_rfu_season_res.df) %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "model") %>% 
  mutate(model = case_when(model == "...1" ~ "best_AIC",
                           TRUE ~ model)) %>% 
  select(model, AICc, R.2, pred_test_error, 
         sensor_rfu, rfu_temp_corrected, everything()) %>% 
  select(-c(delta, weight))

Summary Table for main models

You need reserve. Season helps, but primarily, you need reserve. Tweaking beyond that with temperature-correcting RFU, including turbidity and/or FDOM, etc., could improve things. But including ‘Reserve’ has the most impact on the model, repeatedly. So if you want a really good model, you have to put in some work to get the samples at your reserve.

Models: Individual Reserves; Tank + ISCO

load(here::here("data", "subset_no_NA.RData"))

options(na.action = "na.fail")

Modeling: Individual Reserves, Tank + ISCO

Each of the models described below are fitted and evaluated using symmetric Median Absolute Percent Error.

Full Model

Includes all interactions between sensor_rfu, turbidity, and FDOM. Additionally, temp*rfu and temp*fdom. Hoping we can actually drop some of these.

Reserve included as fixed effect.

response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season + reserve

No FDOM

If we drop FDOM and all its interactions, what do we get?

NOTE this still includes both reserve and season (as well as sensor readings from temp and turbidity)

RFU only

This does not include reserve or season. If the other models above are better, reserve or season could still be the reason (vs. turbidity/temp/FDOM corrections). It would mean local factors still have to be accounted for and modelled to get the most out of a TAL sensor.

Using leave-one-out cross-validation due to low number of samples for some reserves and potential to introduce new factor levels on validation set.

mod_sel_out <- list()
mod_summs_out <- list()
reserves <- unique(dat$reserve)
set.seed(1216)

for(i in seq_along(reserves)){
    res <- dat %>% 
        filter(reserve == reserves[i])

    if(length(unique(res$season))>=2){  
        
        full_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season, data = res)
        no_fdom_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season, data = res)
        no_fdom_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season, data = res)
                           
                           } else {
                               
            full_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp, data = res)
            
            no_fdom_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp, data = res)
            no_fdom_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp, data = res)
        }
    
    rfu_only <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = res)
    rfu_only_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = res)
    
    sel <- dredge(full_ols, 
                  fixed = "sensor_rfu",
                  extra = c("R^2", "AdjR^2" = function(x) summary(x)$adj.r.squared))
    
    # perform cross-validation on top model to find median prediction error
    ols.1 <- get.models(sel, 1)[[1]]
    ols.cv <- cv.glm(res, ols.1, cost)
    
    no_fdom.cv <- cv.glm(res, no_fdom_ols, cost)
    no_fdom.df <- data.frame(model.sel(no_fdom_ols))
    no_fdom.df$pred_test_error <- round(no_fdom.cv$delta[1], 2)
    
    rfu_only.cv <- cv.glm(res, rfu_only, cost)
    rfu_only.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_only))
    rfu_only.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_only.cv$delta[1], 2)
    
    # pull out R^2s from lms (glms were run for cross-validation but really they're just regular linear models)
    no_fdom.df$R.2 <- round(summary(no_fdom_lm)$r.squared, 4)
    rfu_only.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_only_lm)$r.squared, 4)
    

    # see anything with delta AICc < 2
    # subdf <- data.frame(subset(sel, delta < 2))
    
    # only top one
    subdf <- data.frame(sel[1])
    subdf$pred_test_error <- round(ols.cv$delta[1], 2)
    subdf <- subdf %>% 
      bind_rows(no_fdom.df, rfu_only.df) %>% 
      rownames_to_column(var = "model") %>% 
      mutate(model = case_when(model == "...1" ~ "best_AIC",
                               TRUE ~ model)) %>% 
      select(model, AICc, R.2, pred_test_error, everything()) %>% 
      select(-c(delta, weight))
    
    # attach prediction error to it
    mod_sel_out[[i]] <- subdf
    
    # summary for top model
    mod_summs_out[[i]] <- summary(ols.1)
    
      
}
mod_sel_out <- purrr::set_names(mod_sel_out, reserves)
mod_summs_out <- purrr::set_names(mod_summs_out, reserves)

Models: Individual Reserves; Tank Only

load(here::here("data", "subset_no_NA.RData"))
table(dat$method)
## 
## isco tank 
##  765  311
dat_isco <- filter(dat, method == "isco")
dat <- filter(dat, method == "tank")

# subset isco data to only reserves that also have tank data
dat_isco <- dat_isco %>% 
  filter(reserve %in% unique(dat$reserve))

# original plot settings, for later
op <- par()

# options, for MuMIn operations
# will prevent fitting sub-models to different datasets (from help file)
options(na.action = "na.fail")
dat$response <- sqrt(dat$extracted)

Modeling: Individual Reserves, Tank Only

Each of the models described below are fitted and evaluated using symmetric Median Absolute Percent Error.

Full Model

Includes all interactions between sensor_rfu, turbidity, and FDOM. Additionally, temp*rfu and temp*fdom. Hoping we can actually drop some of these.

Reserve included as fixed effect.

response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season + reserve

No FDOM

If we drop FDOM and all its interactions, what do we get?

NOTE this still includes both reserve and season (as well as sensor readings from temp and turbidity)

RFU only

This does not include reserve or season. If the other models above are better, reserve or season could still be the reason (vs. turbidity/temp/FDOM corrections). It would mean local factors still have to be accounted for and modelled to get the most out of a TAL sensor.

RFU + season

Temp-Corrected RFU + season

Temp-corrected RFU is denoted as tc_rfu in the model names and objects. The correction was based on a global rho value which was the average of all individual rho values, as calculated by Hannah Ramage, from the temperature interference trials. This global rho value was then inserted into the equation from Watras et al. 2017 as follows:

Temp-corrected-RFU = original-RFU / (1 + global_rho*(temp_reading - 20))

Using leave-one-out cross-validation due to low number of samples for some reserves and potential to introduce new factor levels on validation set.

Testing predictions on ISCO data

Five reserves collected both tank and ISCO data: GND, GTM, LKS, PDB, GRB. (NIW is not included here because their ISCO data was collected at a different station than their tank data.)

For these reserves, we will see how well predictions from the three core models built from tank data compare to the observed ISCO data.

mod_sel_out <- list()
mod_summs_out <- list()
isco_preds_out <- list()
reserves <- unique(dat$reserve)
set.seed(1216)

for(i in seq_along(reserves)){
    res <- dat %>% 
        filter(reserve == reserves[i])

    if(length(unique(res$season))>=2){  
        #lots of variables  
        full_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp + season, data = res)
        # remove FDOM
        no_fdom_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season, data = res)
        no_fdom_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + season, data = res)
        # only rfu + season
        rfu_season <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + season, data = res)
        rfu_season_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + season, data = res)
        # cross-validate
        rfu_season.cv <- cv.glm(res, rfu_season, cost)
        rfu_season.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_season))
        rfu_season.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_season.cv$delta[1], 2)
        rfu_season.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_season_lm)$r.squared, 4)
        # temp-corrected rfu + season
        tc_rfu_season <- glm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + season, data = res)
        tc_rfu_season_lm <- lm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected + season, data = res)
        # cross-validate
        tc_rfu_season.cv <- cv.glm(res, tc_rfu_season, cost)
        tc_rfu_season.df <- data.frame(model.sel(tc_rfu_season))
        tc_rfu_season.df$pred_test_error <- round(tc_rfu_season.cv$delta[1], 2)
        tc_rfu_season.df$R.2 <- round(summary(tc_rfu_season_lm)$r.squared, 4)
                           
                           } else {
                               
            full_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb + fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb*fdom_qsu + sensor_rfu*turb + sensor_rfu*fdom_qsu + turb*fdom_qsu + temp + sensor_rfu*temp + fdom_qsu*temp, data = res)
            
            no_fdom_ols <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp, data = res)
            no_fdom_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu + turb +  sensor_rfu*turb + temp + sensor_rfu*temp, data = res)
        }
    
    rfu_only <- glm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = res)
    rfu_only_lm <- lm(response ~ sensor_rfu, data = res)
    
    tc_rfu_only <- glm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected, data = res)
    tc_rfu_only_lm <- lm(response ~ rfu_temp_corrected, data = res)
    
    sel <- dredge(full_ols, 
                  fixed = "sensor_rfu",
                  extra = c("R^2", "AdjR^2" = function(x) summary(x)$adj.r.squared))
    
    # perform cross-validation on top model to find median prediction error
    ols.1 <- get.models(sel, 1)[[1]]
    ols.cv <- cv.glm(res, ols.1, cost)
    
    no_fdom.cv <- cv.glm(res, no_fdom_ols, cost)
    no_fdom.df <- data.frame(model.sel(no_fdom_ols))
    no_fdom.df$pred_test_error <- round(no_fdom.cv$delta[1], 2)
    
    rfu_only.cv <- cv.glm(res, rfu_only, cost)
    rfu_only.df <- data.frame(model.sel(rfu_only))
    rfu_only.df$pred_test_error <- round(rfu_only.cv$delta[1], 2)
    
    tc_rfu_only.cv <- cv.glm(res, tc_rfu_only, cost)
    tc_rfu_only.df <- data.frame(model.sel(tc_rfu_only))
    tc_rfu_only.df$pred_test_error <- round(tc_rfu_only.cv$delta[1], 2)
    
    # pull out R^2s from lms (glms were run for cross-validation but really they're just regular linear models)
    no_fdom.df$R.2 <- round(summary(no_fdom_lm)$r.squared, 4)
    rfu_only.df$R.2 <- round(summary(rfu_only_lm)$r.squared, 4)
    tc_rfu_only.df$R.2 <- round(summary(tc_rfu_only_lm)$r.squared, 4)

    
    ## BIND IT ALL TOGETHER
    
    # only top one
    subdf <- data.frame(sel[1])
    subdf$pred_test_error <- round(ols.cv$delta[1], 2)
    
    # if seasonal models exist, add them to this df
    if(length(unique(res$season))>=2){
      subdf <- subdf %>% 
        bind_rows(rfu_season.df, tc_rfu_season.df)
    }
    
    # bind other data frames of output and format
    subdf <- subdf %>% 
      bind_rows(no_fdom.df, rfu_only.df, tc_rfu_only.df) %>% 
      rownames_to_column(var = "model") %>% 
      mutate(model = case_when(model == "...1" ~ "best_AIC",
                               TRUE ~ model)) %>% 
      select(model, AICc, R.2, pred_test_error, everything()) %>% 
      select(-c(delta, weight))
    
    # attach prediction error to it
    mod_sel_out[[i]] <- subdf
    
    # summary for top model
    mod_summs_out[[i]] <- summary(ols.1)
    
    
    # ISCO predictions 
    if(reserves[i] %in% unique(dat_isco$reserve)){
      isco <- dat_isco %>% 
        filter(reserve == reserves[i],
               season %in% unique(res$season)) %>% 
        mutate(preds_best_AIC = (predict(ols.1, newdata = .))^2,
               preds_no_fdom_ols = (predict(no_fdom_ols, newdata = .))^2,
               preds_rfu_only = (predict(rfu_only, newdata = .))^2)
      
      isco_preds_out[[i]] <- isco
      
      
    }
    
      
}
mod_sel_out <- purrr::set_names(mod_sel_out, reserves)
mod_summs_out <- purrr::set_names(mod_summs_out, reserves)
isco_preds <- bind_rows(isco_preds_out)
isco_preds_long <- isco_preds %>% 
  select(reserve, month, season, method, extracted, starts_with("preds")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("preds"),
               names_to = "model",
               names_prefix = "preds_",
               values_to = "predicted")

Summary Table

           across(c(R.2, sensor_rfu, rfu_temp_corrected, X.Intercept.), round, 3),
           across(c(fdom_qsu, turb, temp), round, 4),
           across(c(fdom_qsu.sensor_rfu:fdom_qsu.sensor_rfu.turb), round, 4) )

Graph of model diagnostics by reserve

diags <- mod_sel_df %>% 
  select(Reserve, model, AICc, R.2, prediction_error) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-c(Reserve, model), names_to = "diagnostic", values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(diagnostic = case_when(diagnostic == "R.2" ~ "R^2",
                                diagnostic == "prediction_error" ~ "Prediction Error",
                                TRUE ~ diagnostic),
         model_type = case_when(stringr::str_starts(model, "rfu") ~ "RFU",
                                stringr::str_starts(model, "tc_rfu") ~ "TC-RFU",
                                TRUE ~ "multi-vars"))
my_shapes <- c(16, 17, 15, 7, 8, 9)

# colors below are from khroma::muted and are colorblind-friendly
# though that's not really necessary here because we also have shapes and names

ggplot(diags, aes(x = value, y = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(color = model_type, shape = model)) +
  facet_grid(Reserve~diagnostic, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(my_shapes, 2)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#332288", "#882255", "#44AA99")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("Reserve models; Tank data only")

Get rid of GND and PDB due to that massive overfitting that messes up the AICc scale, and also HEE_w2 because it was such a small sample size.

diags %>% 
  filter(!(Reserve %in% c("GND", "PDB", "HEE_w2"))) %>% 
ggplot(aes(x = value, y = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(color = model_type, shape = model)) +
  facet_grid(Reserve~diagnostic, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(my_shapes, 2)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#332288", "#882255", "#44AA99")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("Reserve models; Tank data only")

Same thing, but also get rid of temp-corrected RFU because it adds clutter.

diags %>% 
  filter(!(Reserve %in% c("GND", "PDB", "HEE_w2")),
         !(model %in% c("tc_rfu_season", "tc_rfu_only"))) %>% 
ggplot(aes(x = value, y = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(color = model_type, shape = model)) +
  facet_grid(Reserve~diagnostic, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(my_shapes, 2)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#332288", "#882255", "#44AA99")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle("Reserve models; Tank data only")

ggsave(here::here("model_figures", 
                  "IndRes_TankOnly_4Mods_diagnostics.png"),
       width = 6, height = 7, units = "in")
ggplot(mod_sel_df, aes(x = prediction_error, y = model,
                       color = model, shape = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~Reserve)

Graphs of ISCO predictions

ggplot(isco_preds_long) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
  geom_point(aes(x = predicted, y = extracted, color = reserve, shape = model),
             alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(title = "Observed ISCO by predictions from tank models",
       subtitle = "Gray line on each panel is 1:1 line")

ggplot(isco_preds_long) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
  geom_point(aes(x = predicted, y = extracted, color = model, shape = model),
             alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~reserve) +
  labs(title = "Observed ISCO by predictions from tank models",
       subtitle = "Gray line on each panel is 1:1 line")

ggplot(isco_preds_long) +

  geom_point(aes(x = predicted, y = extracted, color = model, shape = model),

Graphic: R^2 and prediction error for all models

Reserve code ‘ALL’ represents the combined-reserve models.

files_allRes <- c("AllRes_TankAndISCO", "AllRes_TankOnly")
files_indRes <- c("IndRes_TankAndISCO", "IndRes_TankOnly")
# read in Individual Reserve data frames
dat_ind_ti <- read_csv(here::here("model_coeffs",
                           paste0(files_indRes[[1]], ".csv")))

dat_ind_t <- read_csv(here::here("model_coeffs",
                           paste0(files_indRes[[2]], ".csv")))

# combine for faceting
dat_ind_t$data_source <- "Tank Only"
dat_ind_ti$data_source <- "Tank + ISCO"

dat_all <- bind_rows(dat_ind_t, dat_ind_ti)
# all reserves
all_ti <- read_csv(here::here("model_coeffs",
                           paste0(files_allRes[[1]], ".csv")))

all_t <- read_csv(here::here("model_coeffs",
                           paste0(files_allRes[[2]], ".csv")))
all_t <- all_t %>% 
  mutate(data_source = "Tank Only",
         Reserve = 'ALL')

all_ti <- all_ti %>% 
  mutate(data_source = "Tank + ISCO",
         Reserve = 'ALL')

dat_all <- bind_rows(dat_all, all_t, all_ti)
# main 3 models: best_AIC, no_fdom_ols, rfu_only
dat_main3 <- dat_all %>% 
  filter(model %in% c("best_AIC", "no_fdom_ols", "rfu_only"))

# other potential biggies: rfu_season, rfu_reserve
dat_main5 <- dat_all %>% 
  filter(model %in% c("best_AIC", "no_fdom_ols", "rfu_only",
                      "rfu_season", "rfu_reserve"))

Main 3 models

Original diagnostic plot

rsq <- ggplot(dat_main3,
       aes(x = Reserve,
           y = R.2,
           color = model,
           shape = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3,
             alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~data_source) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("R"^"2"))

err <- ggplot(dat_main3,
       aes(x = Reserve,
           y = prediction_error,
           color = model,
           shape = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3,
             alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~data_source) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Median Absolute \nPrediction Error")
# try adding labels with some code from the stackoverflow answer
# https://stackoverflow.com/a/60354844
col1 <- ggplot() + annotate(geom = 'text', x=1, y=1, label="Tank + ISCO") + theme_void() 

col2 <- ggplot() + annotate(geom = 'text', x=1, y=1, label="Tank Only") + theme_void() 


# from khroma::vibrant
colors <- scale_color_manual(values = rep(c("#0077BB", "#CC3311", "#009988"), 4))

(col1 + col2) / (rsq + colors) / (err + colors) +
  plot_layout(guides = 'collect',
              heights = c(1, 3, 3))

ggsave(here::here("model_figures", "diagnostic_plot_main3models.png"),
       width = 8.5, height = 6.5, units = "in")
